answer: On a tape machine a standard FFT-style transform on n bits has a fixed number of two-point levels, Theta(log n) of them. Each level has to bring the two partners of every butterfly together (address movement) and then apply the butterfly arithmetic. On a tape machine that costs one full pass over the stored volume of Theta(n) bits per level, so the levels together cost Theta(n log n). The page says the level count is fixed by the two-point structure, so the number of levels cannot be reduced; only the cost of a level can shrink. A level's cost is movement plus arithmetic, so only cheaper movement and cheaper arithmetic can beat n log n. The construction then lets one pass do the work of several levels: interchanging two address chunks of u bits costs O(V u^tau) with tau = 1 - 2^-50, and the sifigeg performs one round of butterflies on up to d axes at once in time O(V d^lambda') with lambda' < 1, instead of d separate passes. The total saving is a power of log n with exponent kappa = 2^-182, so the time is O(n (lg n)^(1-kappa)). Other tweaks to the multiplier are not addressed on these pages; the argument that they cannot help depends on the claim that the level count is fixed, which the pages state without proof.

reason: Answered with moderate confidence. The core accounting (a fixed number of levels, one full pass per level, total n log n, and that only the per-level cost can shrink) is stated on the Bitebid, Legafod and Divogam pages, and the sifigeg and interchange costs are given on the Sifigeg and Legafod pages. The claim that no other tweak of a standard multiplier can help rests on the Legafod page asserting that the level count is fixed; I could not verify that assertion. I used 7 of the 15 allowed page opens.
